raw_response:
Well, let me think about this year. I'm 70 now, been farming these 10 mu for half a century. My back isn't what it used to be, but I still know every inch of this land. My two sons work in Handan, send some money back, but they can't help much during the busy season. It's just me and the old woman most of the time, though my nephew sometimes hires on when we need extra hands.

It's mid-October now, time to get the wheat in the ground. The soil is still warm enough and we had decent rain last month, so moisture is okay. I've been doing wheat-maize double cropping on all 10 mu for 30 years — I know the drill. The maize came off fine this September, got about 480 jin per mu. Not great, not terrible. The straw is already chopped and spread.

For the wheat, I'll plant around October 15th. I use the same improved variety I've been using — don't remember the exact name the seed shop calls it, but it's the one with the short stalk that doesn't lodge. I save some seed but I bought fresh this year because my saved seed had some Fusarium last season. Cost about 45 yuan per mu for seed.

Fertilizer-wise, I'll put down compound fertilizer as base — about 25 kg per mu, that's roughly 6 kg P and 6 kg K per mu, plus some N. Then at jointing in March, I'll topdress with about 10 kg of urea per mu, which gives another 10 kg N or so. Total N around 16 kg per mu. I know some of the younger farmers with bigger farms are pushing 20 kg N, but I'm careful. Last year I did 18 kg and the wheat got a bit lush and lodged in that heavy rain in May. Better to be a bit conservative. The compound fertilizer costs about 75 yuan per mu, urea about 25 yuan per mu.

I'll irrigate three times for wheat: once before winter to help establishment, once at jointing in spring, and once at heading. The well water costs money — electricity for the pump runs about 25 yuan each time per mu. Three times is enough if the spring rain is normal. I won't do the fourth irrigation some folks do at grain filling — saves 250 yuan across the whole farm and the yield difference isn't worth it for me.

For pests, I'll spray herbicide once in early spring for weeds — the chickweed and wild oats are always bad. Maybe insecticide if I see aphids at heading, but I won't buy it until I see them. That's 30 yuan per mu for the herbicide.

Then the wheat comes off in early June — always a rush. I'll hire a combine, about 50 yuan per mu. The straw goes back on the field. Immediately after harvest, within 3-4 days, the maize goes in. I can't waste time — the window is tight. I buy hybrid maize seed every year, can't save it. That's 60 yuan per mu. I plant at about 4000 plants per mu, use the planter I share with my cousin.

For maize fertilizer, I put compound fertilizer down at planting — about 20 kg per mu, gives 5 kg P, 5 kg K, and some N. Then at the 10-leaf stage, I topdress with urea, about 8 kg per mu. Total N around 14 kg per mu. I've found going higher doesn't pay on my land — the soil is decent but not rich.

Maize irrigation — I'll do one good irrigation at the big trumpet stage in July if it doesn't rain. Sometimes I need a second if August is dry, but usually once is enough. That's another 25 yuan per mu. I'll spray herbicide once and maybe insecticide if the corn borer is bad. Budget about 40 yuan per mu for chemicals on maize.

Labor: Me and my wife handle most of it, but for harvest and the rushed wheat-maize turnover, I hire my nephew for about 5 days each crop. He charges 150 yuan per day now. So 10 hired days total, 1500 yuan. Family puts in maybe 40 days across the whole year.

Total costs: Wheat seed 450, maize seed 600, fertilizer about 2000 for both crops, irrigation about 750, pesticides about 700, hired labor 1500, machine harvest 500. Total around 6,500 yuan. I expect about 450 kg per mu wheat and 500 kg per mu maize. At current prices that's about 1.1 yuan per jin for wheat, 1.0 yuan for maize. So revenue around 10,500 yuan. Not much left after costs, but it's enough for us old folks, plus what the boys send home.
